page: Vultr vx1-g-64c-256g-3840s is a high-capacity general-purpose cloud instance from the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 64 dedicated virtual CPUs powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz on x86_64 architecture. The underlying hardware exposes 32 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading (2 threads per core), backed by 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 acceleration, alongside AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic instructions.

System memory totals 256.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Large-block uncached memory benchmarks demonstrate strong sustained throughput, reaching 496.98 GB/sec in read operations and 190.5 GB/sec in write operations, both placing in the top ten percent of tested hardware. The instance does not include a GPU, but it bundles 3840 GB of local NVMe SSD storage directly on the node, removing the latency and provisioning overhead associated with attached network volumes.

Benchmark results indicate strong parallel computing and data-handling performance. The server achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 2767.0 and a multi-core score of 27795.0, placing in the top decile. In software compilation with Clang, the system scored 64042.0, while PassMark database operations reached 35622.38. In in-memory data processing, Redis SET operations reached 104.09 million operations per second, supported by multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rates of 458.76 GB/sec and static web serving throughput of 64.48 GB/sec.

In terms of qualitative resource efficiency, combining 64 dedicated cores, 256 GB of RAM, and 3.84 TB of fast local NVMe storage within a single instance provides high compute and storage density. This consolidated configuration minimizes inter-node communication penalties for large workloads. The configuration is well suited for demanding production databases, continuous integration build clusters, large-scale web application serving, and parallel batch data processing.

It provides 256.0 GB of system memory, matching a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio, and bundles 3840 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage without discrete GPU hardware. The server delivers top-tier multi-core computing metrics, reflected by a Geekbench multi-core score of 27795.0 and top-decile Clang software build throughput. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 496.98 GB/sec, while bundled NVMe storage drives high transaction rates in database benchmarks and 104.09 million Redis SET operations per second. The combined density of dedicated compute, sizable memory, and integrated local storage offers efficient multi-threaded capacity for production database systems, large CI/CD pipelines, container orchestration hosts, and heavy web serving tiers.
